Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **The sample in Chinese**, Simplified and Traditional: every demo, the interface, the manual, the credits and the subtitles, drawn in Noto Sans SC and TC. Config's Language row has four buttons, and F9 and the controller's L2 go round all four
- **Fields of several lines** (`[edit multiline=true rows=4]`), with the phone's own keyboard in its multi-line mode, and `KAGAskText` to ask for text in the look of the game's prompts
- **Comments on saves**, as Wamsoft's games take them: with Config's A Comment for Each Save, the game asks after each save, and the save and load screens show the comment in the slot
- **Screenshots into the phone's photo gallery** on Android and iOS (Photos at first; the save folder if the player picks it)
- **A report when the game stops answering**: after 20 seconds the game writes what it was doing, and every thread's state, to `freeze-report.txt` in its save folder and to the system's log, for a player to send
- For games brought from older Kirikiri engines: `Porting.tjs` shows win32dialog.dll's dialogs as dialogs over the game on every platform, and stands in for getLangName.dll and the original engine's data packs; kagex-release takes a game's icon from its old `.exe` or an `.ico`
- Fixed: the second message font (and now the Chinese ones) drew in a system font outside the message window; the help line kept the old language after a switch; a line read aloud whose sound never said it ended counted as a voice for ever (now stopped past its length)
- kagex-release 0.28.1 downloads the 0.28.1 engines

The sample game with Live2D (`kagex_sample_live2d_<platform>`, added to this release once it's out) holds Live2D's Cubism Core: by installing or playing it you agree not to copy the Cubism Core out of it, distribute it apart from the game, modify it, or reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble it. It uses sample data owned and copyrighted by Live2D Inc.

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.28.1/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
